desc: Vindhyachal Super Thermal Power Station is the largest power station in India, located in the Singrauli district of Madhya Pradesh. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 4,760 MW. The plant uses coal from the nearby Nigahi mines and draws water from the Singrauli reservoir. Commissioned in phases starting from 1987, it supplies power to multiple states across northern and western India. The plant spans over 3,500 acres and employs advanced pollution control technologies.
fact: It is the largest power station in India with 4,760 MW capacity · Operated by NTPC, commissioned in phases since 1987 · It uses coal from nearby Nigahi mines · It spans over 3,500 acres and supplies power to multiple states

desc: Mundra Thermal Power Station is a large coal-fired power plant located at Mundra in the Kutch district of Gujarat. Operated by Adani Power, it has an installed capacity of 4,620 MW, making it one of the largest private thermal power plants in India. The plant uses imported coal and is strategically located near Mundra Port for fuel supply. It was commissioned in phases between 2009 and 2012. The plant features supercritical boiler technology for higher efficiency and lower emissions.
fact: It is one of the largest private thermal power plants in India at 4,620 MW · It uses imported coal delivered via Mundra Port · It features supercritical boiler technology for higher efficiency · Commissioned between 2009 and 2012 by Adani Power

desc: Sasan Ultra Mega Power Project (UMPP) is a 3,960 MW coal-fired power plant located in the Singrauli district of Madhya Pradesh. Operated by Reliance Power, it is one of India's first Ultra Mega Power Projects, conceived to benefit from economies of scale. The plant uses supercritical technology and is linked to captive coal mines in the Moher and Chhatrasal coal blocks. Commissioned in 2015, it supplies power to 14 states across India. The project was developed with an investment exceeding ₹25,000 crore.
fact: It is one of India's first Ultra Mega Power Projects at 3,960 MW · It uses supercritical boiler technology with captive coal mines · It supplies power to 14 states across India · Developed by Reliance Power and commissioned in 2015

desc: Singrauli Super Thermal Power Station is a major coal-fired power plant located in the Sonebhadra district of Uttar Pradesh. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 2,000 MW and was commissioned between 1982 and 1991. It was the first super thermal power station in India and the site of NTPC's corporate training institute. The plant shares the Singrauli coalfield region with several other thermal plants and is a key supplier of power to the northern grid.
fact: It was the first super thermal power station in India · Operated by NTPC with 2,000 MW capacity · It hosts NTPC's corporate training institute · Commissioned between 1982 and 1991 in the Singrauli coalfield region

desc: Korba Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located in Korba, Chhattisgarh. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 2,600 MW. The plant is situated in the Korba coalfield region, one of India's largest coal-producing areas. Commissioned in phases from 1983 to 2014, it supplies power to the western and northern regions of India. The plant uses coal from the Korba and South Karanpura coalfields and draws water from the Hasdeo River.

desc: Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located in the Peddapalli district of Telangana. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 2,600 MW. Commissioned between 1983 and 2007, it was the first power plant in India to use the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system. The plant uses coal from nearby mines and draws water from the Godavari River through a pipeline. It is a major supplier of power to the southern region of India.

desc: Talcher Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located in Talcher, Odisha. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 3,000 MW, making it one of the largest thermal power stations in eastern India. The plant is situated in the Talcher coalfield, one of India's largest coal reserves. Commissioned in phases between 1995 and 2025, it uses coal from captive mines. The plant supplies power to the eastern, western, and southern regions and features electrostatic precipitators for emission control.

desc: Chandrapur Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located in Chandrapur, Maharashtra. Operated by MSPGCL, it has an installed capacity of 3,340 MW, making it the largest power station in Maharashtra. The plant uses coal from the Western Coalfields Limited mines in the region. Commissioned in phases from 1979 to 2021, it supplies power primarily to Maharashtra. The plant has undergone several retrofits for emission compliance and features advanced pollution control systems including flue gas desulfurization.

desc: Farakka Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located near Farakka in the Murshidabad district of West Bengal. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 2,100 MW. The plant is strategically located on the banks of the Bhagirathi River and uses coal from the Rajmahal and Eastern Coalfields. Commissioned between 1986 and 2010, it is a key supplier of power to West Bengal and the eastern region. The plant features both conventional and supercritical boiler units.

desc: Rihand Super Thermal Power Station is a coal-fired power plant located in the Sonebhadra district of Uttar Pradesh. Operated by NTPC, it has an installed capacity of 3,000 MW. The plant is named after the Rihand Dam and reservoir, which supplies its water. Commissioned in phases from 1988 to 2014, it is one of the largest power stations in the Singrauli region. The plant uses coal from the Amlori and Khadia mines and supplies power to the northern and western regions of India.
